Mailbox folder chips show one canonical name per enabled role: Inbox, Sent, Drafts, Starred, Unread, Trash, Junk and Archived, plus All Mail or Important when enabled. Sent Items, Sent Mail and casing variants share one Sent chip. Chips stay in a fixed order and belong to the selected mailbox, never a merge of every account's raw folder names. Selecting another folder with the same role keeps that real folder selected; all server folders remain available in the sidebar. Expanded IMAP, Gmail and Outlook accounts share the same colorful folder icons for known roles, with a folder icon for custom folders. Saved account expansion choices are respected. Each connected account has an address-first heading with its saved label or provider below it; Local Folders uses the same layout with On this computer. Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo and custom IMAP share row spacing, icons, unread counts and selection styling. Every account, including Local Folders, indents its first-level folders 14 pixels below the heading; subfolders retain their additional nesting, and unread badges stay right-aligned. Real folder parents keep their expanders and hierarchy. Gmail API system categories and Yellow star use readable names; original names remain in tooltips and folder filtering. Custom names and underlying folder identities stay unchanged. All Account Mail keeps its Inbox, Outbox, Starred and Unread sidebar views; cross-account Sent, Drafts, Trash, Junk and Archived chips are unavailable. Folder chips stay left aligned below a visible title, including All Mail, and wrap within narrow lists.
